angleRead.name: Angela Reyes
angleRead.text: I want to write a short, steady-state piece about the week the schools numbers barely moved. The word that matters is "regular." Most neighborhoods slipped or gained by a hundredth or two. Six slid by about a tenth: Jack London (7.39 to 7.3), Fruitvale (7.3 to 7.2), Grand Lake (7.18 to 7.09), Uptown (7.12 to 7.03), Downtown (7.28 to 7.2) and West Oakland (8.0 to 7.92). Enrollment ticked up by one to three students in nearly every neighborhood. Teacher quality and funding didn't change anywhere. So the question is why the index dipped where nothing else did. I don't know yet whether it's a real change in classrooms, a rounding artifact or a measurement quirk. I'll go at it the way I'd go at a

plan.chase: I want to write a short, steady-state piece about the week the schools numbers barely moved. The word that matters is "regular." Most neighborhoods slipped or gained by a hundredth or two. Six slid by about a tenth: Jack London (7.39 to 7.3), Fruitvale (7.3 to 7.2), Grand Lake (7.18 to 7.09), Uptown (7.12 to 7.03), Downtown (7.28 to 7.2) and West Oakland (8.0 to 7.92). Enrollment ticked up by one to three students in nearly every neighborhood. Teacher quality and funding didn't change anywhere. So the question is why the index dipped where nothing else did. I don't know yet whether it's a real change in classrooms, a rounding artifact or a measurement quirk. I'll go at it the way I'd go at a
plan.focus: Steady schools week: a small index dip in six neighborhoods against flat funding and teacher quality and slightly rising enrollment. I'll check whether the dip reflects anything teachers see in classrooms.
plan.why: My beat is stability. A near-flat week with a consistent tenth-of-a-point slide in six neighborhoods, set against flat funding and teacher quality and rising enrollment, is worth checking. It could be nothing, and saying that clearly is also the story. I haven't found earlier Tribune coverage of this, so I'm treating it as fresh.
checks: Confirm the C116 and C117 index values for all six neighborhoods against the Neighborhood_Demographics sheet.
Ask the Deputy Mayor for community development how the school quality index is built and whether a dip of about 0.1 means anything.
Confirm that funding and teacher quality were unchanged in those neighborhoods.
Check whether the Tribune has covered these neighborhoods' schools before, since the recall search returned nothing.
Verify the enrollment increases are as small as the sheet says before I describe them as growth.

targets.question: You said the calendar squares all look alike lately. What does a regular week look like in your ESL classroom now? Have you noticed anything in attendance, behavior or how new students are settling in?
targets.basis: Fruitvale ESL teacher. Fruitvale's index fell from 7.3 to 7.2 while enrollment rose by one. Her C117 note about sameness could be peace or stagnation.

targets.question: What do you notice first in your elementary classroom these days, and has anything shifted in attendance or mood this fall?
targets.basis: Fruitvale elementary teacher in the same neighborhood as the index dip. She offers a second classroom view.

targets.question: As a creative writing teacher in Jack London, what changes do you see in your students' writing or engagement? Jack London's index slipped from 7.39 to 7.3. Does that match what you see?
targets.basis: Jack London creative writing teacher, age 68. The neighborhood's index fell about 0.09 with only 203 students and funding unchanged.

targets.question: You sit in a lot of meetings and see kids one on one. What are West Oakland students bringing in, and is there a change behind the index slipping from 8.0 to 7.92?
targets.basis: West Oakland youth counselor. The index fell there while enrollment rose by one student.

targets.question: You went from the kitchen to the classroom and argued the team's case at work. How do sports talk and school routines interact for your Fruitvale K-8 students right now?
targets.basis: Fruitvale K-8 teacher and former line cook. He adds a human, team-spirited angle, and Fruitvale is one of the six dipping neighborhoods.

plan.interpretation: A tenth-of-a-point drop in six neighborhoods that otherwise look unchanged could be noise or a lagging indicator. Enrollment is rising slightly and funding hasn't moved, so I don't see a crisis. The more likely story is that regular held, and I need teachers' eyes to confirm it.
unverifiedLead: The dip might come from how the index is calculated rather than anything in classrooms.
Teachers describing sameness (Isabel Lopes) might mean calm, or they might mean stuck. I can't tell which without asking.
The Oakland Alternative Response Initiative may be affecting how safe Jack London families feel, going by Lo Thoop's note, but that is only a hunch.
